## git authorization delete

Forget the caller’s authorization

```bash
nb-studio git authorization delete <connection>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

| Flag    | Type    | Description                                                             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--yes` | boolean | Go ahead without asking “Forget your authorization of this connection?” |

**Output:** Nothing; prints `Done.`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `DELETE /api/git/authorizations/{connectionId}` (`gitDeleteAuthorization`)

## git authorization list

List the caller’s own authorizations on code hosts

The connections the caller can connect their own account through, oldest first, and those they already did (even once a connection stops allowing it, so they can disconnect). Demo connections are never listed.

```bash
nb-studio git authorization list
```

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `GET /api/git/authorizations` (`gitListAuthorizations`)

## git authorization poll

Poll a device flow authorization

Asks the host once whether the caller entered the code, and stores the authorization once they did.

```bash
nb-studio git authorization poll <connection> --handle <string>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

| Flag       | Type   | Description |
| ---------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `--handle` | string | (required)  |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/authorizations/{connectionId}/pollDeviceFlow` (`gitPollDeviceFlow`)

## git authorization start

Start a device flow authorization

Answers the code the caller enters on the host; poll `pollDeviceFlow` with `handle` until it is connected.

```bash
nb-studio git authorization start <connection>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/authorizations/{connectionId}/startDeviceFlow` (`gitStartDeviceFlow`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio git authorization start <connection>
```

## git authorization use-token

Authorize with a personal access token

Checks the token by calling the host as it, then stores it as the caller’s authorization. The token is never sent back.

```bash
nb-studio git authorization use-token <connection> --token <string>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

| Flag      | Type   | Description |
| --------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `--token` | string | (required)  |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/authorizations/{connectionId}/useToken` (`gitUsePersonalToken`)

## git connection create

Add a connection to a code host

For whoever manages the connections. `sameAppAs` adds another installation of an existing app connection, taking its credentials.

```bash
nb-studio git connection create
```

| Flag                      | Type    | Description                    |
| ------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------ |
| `--provider`              | github  |                                |
| `--kind`                  | app \\  | token                          |     |
| `--same-app-as`           | string  |                                |
| `--name`                  | string  |                                |
| `--web-url`               | string  |                                |
| `--account`               | string  |                                |
| `--app-id`                | string  |                                |
| `--installation-id`       | string  |                                |
| `--client-id`             | string  |                                |
| `--private-key`           | string  | (or --private-key-file <path>) |
| `--client-secret`         | string  |                                |
| `--token`                 | string  |                                |
| `--webhook-secret`        | string  |                                |
| `--allow-personal-tokens` | boolean |                                |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/connections` (`gitCreateConnection`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio git connection create --kind token --name GitHub --account acme --token ghp_...
```

## git connection delete

Remove a connection to a code host

For whoever manages the connections. Everyone’s authorization of it goes too.

```bash
nb-studio git connection delete <connection>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

| Flag    | Type    | Description                                                                                |
| ------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `--yes` | boolean | Go ahead without asking “Remove this connection? Everyone’s authorization of it goes too.” |

**Output:** Nothing; prints `Done.`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `DELETE /api/git/connections/{connectionId}` (`gitDeleteConnection`)

## git connection list

List the connections to code hosts

For whoever may read the git settings. A bounded list; credentials are write-only.

```bash
nb-studio git connection list
```

**Output:** A list (table columns: `id`, `name`, `kind`, `account`, `webUrl`, `usedBy`); with `--json`, `result.data` is the array and `result.meta` the paging.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `GET /api/git/connections` (`gitListConnections`)

## git connection usage

List the repositories linked through a connection

For whoever may read the git settings: the projects’ working directories that link a repository through the connection, which its `usedBy` counts by repository. A bounded list.


| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

**Output:** A list (table columns: `repo`, `projectName`, `resourceId`); with `--json`, `result.data` is the array and `result.meta` the paging.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `GET /api/git/connections/{connectionId}/usage` (`gitListConnectionUses`)

## git repo create

Create a repository on the code host

For whoever manages a project or the connections. `empty` creates it without an initial commit.

```bash
nb-studio git repo create <connection> --name <string> --private
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

| Flag            | Type    | Description |
| --------------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `--owner`       | string  |             |
| `--name`        | string  | (required)  |
| `--private`     | boolean | (required)  |
| `--description` | string  |             |
| `--empty`       | boolean |             |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `POST /api/git/connections/{connectionId}/repositories` (`gitCreateRepository`)

**Examples:**

```bash
nb-studio git repo create <connection> --owner acme --name web --private
```

## git template get

Check a template repository

For whoever may create projects or link repositories: the repository read through the connection, any it can read — a public template of another account included — when it is a template repository. 404 `TEMPLATE_REPO_NOT_FOUND` when the connection cannot read it, 400 `NOT_A_TEMPLATE_REPO` when it is not a template.

```bash
nb-studio git template get <connection> <owner> <name>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |
| `owner`      |             |
| `name`       |             |

**Output:** One record, field by field; with `--json`, `result.data`.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `GET /api/git/connections/{connectionId}/templateRepositories/{owner}/{name}` (`gitGetTemplateRepository`)

## git template list

List the template repositories a connection reaches

For whoever may create projects or link repositories; read live from the code host, one page of the repositories the connection reaches per request, keeping its template repositories (whose name holds `q`, when given). A page may hold none while `meta.nextPageToken` says there are more to read.

```bash
nb-studio git template list <connection>
```

| Argument     | Description |
| ------------ | ----------- |
| `connection` |             |

| Flag           | Type   | Description |
| -------------- | ------ | ----------- |
| `--search`     | string |             |
| `--page-token` | string |             |

**Output:** A list (table columns: `fullName`, `private`, `defaultBranch`, `description`); with `--json`, `result.data` is the array and `result.meta` the paging.

**Who:** People (a sign-in or an API key).

**Request:** `GET /api/git/connections/{connectionId}/templateRepositories` (`gitListTemplateRepositories`)
